Summary: Turn a project idea, existing app, or strategy request into a grounded business plan with financial assumptions, marketing plan, risks, and explicit next actions.
ValueStatement: Support non-code planning work with the same governed artifact handoffs used by software delivery processes.
InterfaceContractSummary: Business strategy hands assumptions to finance and marketing, then consolidates a decision-ready plan.
GovernanceNotes: Claims, forecasts, and channel plans must distinguish sourced facts from assumptions.
ChangeSummary: Introduces a non-coding baseline process for business-plan scenarios and multi-agent handoffs.
GovernancePolicySummary: Proceed only when strategic assumptions, financial drivers, marketing hypotheses, and open risks are explicit.
ConstitutionRuleSummary: Do not hide missing data behind confident plans or unsupported forecasts.
OperatingModeSummary: Assisted execution with agent-owned artifacts and review gates.
SimulationReadinessSummary: Designed for deterministic template projection and real agent handoff validation across business, finance, and marketing specialists.
Metrics: Business plans with explicit assumption inventory.
Existing app or product evidence reviewed before business-case synthesis.
Forecasts that identify drivers, formulas, and confidence.
Marketing plans tied to named customer segments and experiments.
Strategy reviews blocked because critical facts are missing.
Downstream handoffs completed without re-asking for source context.
Risks: Market claims are treated as proven without evidence.
Financial projections use a single precise number despite uncertain inputs.
Marketing plan uses generic channels without segment fit.
Final plan blends assumptions, hypotheses, and facts without labels.
TailoringRules: For existing apps, include a product evidence review before drafting the plan.
For internal projects, marketing work may focus on change-management messaging instead of external channels.
For early ideas, finance should produce ranges and break-even drivers instead of detailed forecasts.
If source data includes spreadsheets, the financial strategist must inspect them before modeling.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Own the business plan spine, operating assumptions, strategic options, and final synthesis.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: An agent or person who can convert ambiguous ideas into decision-ready planning artifacts.
RoleUsages.Notes: Primary owner for strategy framing and integrated plan review.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Own financial assumptions, model logic, unit economics, and sensitivity ranges.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: An agent or person who can turn strategy assumptions and spreadsheet evidence into credible financial planning artifacts.
RoleUsages.Notes: Financial planning owner for model, budget, and sensitivity evidence.

RoleUsages.Purpose: Own positioning, audience, channel mix, campaign brief, and validation experiments.
RoleUsages.StaffingIntent: An agent or person who can convert the business plan into practical go-to-market hypotheses and launch actions.
RoleUsages.Notes: Marketing owner for positioning, messaging, and experiment design.

Steps.Title: Capture strategy intake
Steps.Subtitle: Idea framing and source-material inventory
Steps.Notes: Convert the request into a planning brief with objective, customer segment, constraints, source data, and unknowns.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Project idea, stakeholder ask, source documents, spreadsheets, emails, or existing notes.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Strategy brief and assumption inventory ready for finance and marketing work.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Brief identifies facts, assumptions, open questions, and artifact destination folder.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Business strategist can frame the plan but cannot invent missing source facts.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block when the request lacks a project objective or target audience.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind to another strategy owner if the original owner cannot access source materials.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Business strategy intake brief
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for financial modeling, marketing planning, and final review.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must separate facts, assumptions, open questions, and source-material paths.

Steps.Title: Review product evidence
Steps.Subtitle: Existing app, workflow, or product-context assessment
Steps.Notes: Inspect available product evidence such as an existing app folder, screenshots, README, demo notes, logs, user workflow notes, or generated validation output before drafting the business case.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Strategy brief, source app or product evidence path, screenshots, validation notes, and known operating constraints.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Product evidence assessment ready for business-plan, finance, and marketing work.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Assessment separates observed product capabilities, user value hypotheses, limitations, proof gaps, and assumptions.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Business strategist owns synthesis and must label what was directly observed versus inferred.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block when the source app or product evidence cannot be inspected and the plan depends on it.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Strategy owner remains accountable for separating observed product facts from inferred market claims.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Product evidence assessment
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for business-plan, financial, marketing, and future product-improvement decisions.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must separate observed product behavior, source paths, assumptions, limitations, and validation gaps.

Steps.Title: Draft business plan
Steps.Subtitle: Customer, offer, model, and risk framing
Steps.Notes: Create a concise business plan with target segment, problem, offer, differentiation, operating model, risks, validation plan, and explicit links to source product evidence when present.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Strategy brief, assumption inventory, and product evidence assessment.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Business plan ready for financial and marketing specialization.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Plan contains strategy spine, observed product evidence, assumptions, risks, and open questions.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Business strategist owns plan draft but flags unsupported market claims.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not fabricate customers, competitors, pricing, or market size.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Strategy owner stays accountable for assumptions even when downstream specialists refine them.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Business plan
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for finance, marketing, funding, and execution planning.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include customer segment, problem, offer, differentiation, channels, operating model, risks, and validation plan.

Steps.Title: Model financial assumptions
Steps.Subtitle: Unit economics, budget, and sensitivity
Steps.Notes: Create financial model evidence from the business plan, spreadsheets, and stated assumptions.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Business plan, source spreadsheets, pricing notes, and cost assumptions.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Financial model with drivers, ranges, and sensitivity findings.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Model identifies formulas, units, currency, confidence, and missing data.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Financial strategist owns model logic and must flag unsupported numbers.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not produce precise forecasts without assumptions and sensitivity ranges.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind to another finance owner when spreadsheet access or modeling skills are unavailable.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Financial model and sensitivity note
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for budget planning, pricing decisions, and integrated strategy review.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must show drivers, formulas or calculation logic, ranges, assumptions, and data gaps.

Steps.Title: Prepare marketing plan
Steps.Subtitle: Positioning, channels, and experiments
Steps.Notes: Create go-to-market plan from the business plan and finance constraints.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Positioning, channel plan, campaign brief, and validation experiments.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Marketing plan ties audience, promise, channels, budget dependencies, and metrics to the strategy.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Marketing specialist owns messaging and experiments while calling out unvalidated claims.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not invent proof, testimonials, or customer logos.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Rebind to another marketing owner if the plan needs channel expertise the assigned owner lacks.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Go-to-market and experiment plan
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for launch planning, campaign creation, and customer validation.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must include audience, pain point, promise, proof needs, channels, sequence, metrics, and experiment plan.

Steps.Title: Review integrated business plan
Steps.Subtitle: Decision-ready synthesis and handoff
Steps.Notes: Consolidate strategy, finance, and marketing outputs into one decision-ready package with risks and next actions.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Business plan, financial model, and go-to-market plan.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Integrated plan approved, blocked, or returned for specific corrections.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Review note identifies decision status, assumptions, risks, and next actions.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Business strategist recommends; governance owner approves or blocks the plan.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Block when finance and marketing assumptions conflict or critical source data is missing.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Approval must remain with a strategy owner who has reviewed all upstream artifacts.
Finance review remains required when model assumptions change.
Marketing review remains required when audience, channel, or messaging assumptions change.

ArtifactExpectations.Title: Integrated business plan review
ArtifactExpectations.AllowedFutureUsageSummary: Reusable for execution planning, budget review, and later portfolio decisions.
ArtifactExpectations.ValidationRequirementSummary: Must reconcile strategy, finance, marketing, risks, blockers, and next actions.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Approved
BranchOutcomes.Description: Plan is decision-ready with explicit assumptions and next actions.

BranchOutcomes.Title: Blocked
BranchOutcomes.Description: Plan requires source-data, finance, or marketing correction before approval.

Steps.Title: Publish approved plan handoff
Steps.Subtitle: Decision-ready package for execution
Steps.Notes: Confirm the approved business plan package is ready for execution planning, budget review, or portfolio handoff.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Approved integrated plan review and all upstream strategy, finance, and marketing artifacts.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Approved package is ready for downstream execution planning.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Handoff preserves the decision status, source artifacts, open risks, and named next actions.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Business strategist owns the handoff; finance and marketing owners remain accountable for their assumptions.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not hand off an approved plan when required assumptions or next actions are missing.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Approved handoff remains owned by the strategy owner.
Finance owner confirms downstream users understand financial assumptions.
Marketing owner confirms downstream users understand audience and channel assumptions.

Steps.Title: Capture blocked-plan corrections
Steps.Subtitle: Specific fixes before another review
Steps.Notes: Record why the plan was blocked and which source-data, financial, or marketing corrections are required before another review.
Steps.InputContractSummary: Blocked integrated plan review and all upstream artifacts.
Steps.OutputContractSummary: Blocked status is durable with correction owners and revisit criteria.
Steps.EvidenceContractSummary: Correction plan names missing evidence, conflicting assumptions, owners, and expected next review trigger.
Steps.DecisionRightsSummary: Business strategist records the block; specialists own corrections in their domains.
Steps.ExceptionPolicySummary: Do not block without concrete correction criteria.

RoleAssignments.RebindPolicySummary: Blocked correction plan remains owned by the strategy owner.
Finance owner owns correction criteria for financial assumptions.
Marketing owner owns correction criteria for audience, channel, and messaging assumptions.
